Find: visual reference

The rendered companion to README.md in this folder. Every state the specification names, drawn once, in both themes, at real sizes.

Theme
This is a picture, not a specification. Where this file and README.md disagree, the README wins and this file is the defect. Requirement numbers are cited throughout so each exhibit can be traced back.
0. What revision 1 permitted A. The trailing cluster B. Control homes C. The four presentations D. The zero result E. The inline editor F. The duplicate guard G. Counts H. Recovery I. Both themes

0What revision 1 permitted

An implementation built from revision 1 of the specification. It satisfies every requirement as written. Section 3.1 of the spec exists because of it, and this exhibit is the reason revision 2 was necessary.

The fault is the specification's, not the implementer's. Revision 1 said what the editor contains and in what order. It said nothing about how many boxes that content may sit inside, or how tall it may be. A specification written that way gets built as a box per noun, and every reading below is a reasonable one.
The same editor under revision 2budget 400 px

Same content, same statements, same two actions. One container, used once, and only when there is an ancestor chain worth drawing. Here there is not, so the ancestry is one line. FND-121 to FND-136

AThe trailing cluster

Five controls shared one trailing slot and nothing decided which of them deserved permanent space. FND-86, FND-89

After

The query row is now four slots that never wrap. Clear and Recent searches moved inside the field, Reset moved to the rail header where scope lives, match mode and page size moved to More, and the graph action moved to the results header beside the thing it acts on.

Every frame on this page is resizable from its lower right corner. Drag one and the presentation re-tiers from its own measured rectangle, which is the mechanism FND-96 requires.

BControl homes

Each control sits with the thing it acts on. FND-86

  1. 1Scope entry. Query row, leading. Opens configuration, and states both ratios on its own face so the condition behind a zero result is readable without opening anything. Absent in Expanded, where the rail is a column. FND-29, FND-98
  2. 2Clear. Inside the field, trailing. Acts on the field's text. Absent when the field is empty, not disabled. FND-87
  3. 3Recent searches. Inside the field, trailing. Produces text for the field, so it travels with the field. FND-89
  4. 4Sort. Query row, trailing. Orders the list the field produces. Its visible label drops before the control does. FND-89
  5. 5More. Holds match mode and page size, both changed rarely. Stays in More at every size. FND-89, FND-90
  6. 6Reset filters. Scope rail header. It resets scope, not the query, so it belongs with scope. Absent while scope, match mode and sort are all at their defaults. FND-30
  7. 7The results header action slot. One slot, one action, decided by the result count. With results it carries the graph action. With none it is empty: there is nothing to send to a graph, and the body below already carries creation, so a button here would duplicate it. FND-91, FND-92

CThe four presentations

Four presentations, two thresholds, no new names and no new numbers. Switching happens at 600 wide and 400 high, with exits at 616 and 416 so the mode cannot oscillate at a boundary. FND-95

Folding, not hiding. A column that leaves does not take its value with it. Synonym folds into the entity cell in Narrow, and Type joins it in Narrow and shallow. Read the second and fourth frames above: the data is still on screen. FND-101, FND-102

DThe zero result

The zero state does two jobs in a fixed order: establish whether the entity is genuinely absent, then make creating it trivial. Offering creation before the user has ruled out a scoped miss manufactures duplicates. FND-49

Remedy states

Each remedy carries its own precomputed yield, so the user never clicks hopefully. A remedy that would still yield nothing stays visible and goes disabled with its zero showing, because the zero is itself the diagnostic. A remedy whose change is already in effect is not rendered at all. FND-53, FND-54, FND-55

Left to right: enabled with a real yield, enabled with a real yield, visible and disabled at zero, and the full reset. Cheapest correction first.

When every remedy yields zero

A row of disabled zeroes is not a diagnostic, it is a dead band. The ladder is not rendered at all; one line says the same thing. FND-134

Nothing matched in 2 of 16 fields.

Widening the scope would not help.

Compare with shot: 06, which renders Search all 16 fields  0 matches and Reset every filter  0 matches side by side, both disabled, in a band 56 pixels tall that tells the user nothing they can act on.

EThe inline editor

The two paths are additive, not alternatives. The inline editor handles the common case. Continue in Add entity handles nested parent creation and everything the inline editor does not cover. Deleting the inline editor in favour of the escalation alone removes the common case to serve the rare one. FND-58, FND-59
Room for the editor560 × 620
Collapsed560 × 300

With a real ancestor chain

The ancestry container, its accent rule and its tinted ground appear only here, where there is a chain to draw. The chain is vertical, matching shot: 05. One extra statement row and two extra cards is the entire difference from the collapsed form. FND-62, FND-123, FND-132

One creation affordance at any size. Where there is height the editor is open inline, because the user already said what they wanted by searching for it. Where there is not, it collapses to a button that opens the editor over the body, the way Options does. The two are never both on screen. FND-60, FND-94

An individual's parent is written as a second rdf:type statement, not as rdfs:subClassOf. FND-70

FThe duplicate guard

The check reads every entity in the store, including hidden and generated ones, and ignores the active search scope entirely. The user arrived here because a scoped search found nothing; checking for collisions within that same scope would reproduce the error that sent them here. FND-73, FND-74

Synaptic Plasticity already exists under Course › Science › Biology › Neuroscience.

Exact label collision. Blocks commit. Names the colliding entity with its path and offers to open it, which widens the scope enough to reveal it and selects it. FND-75, FND-76

synaptic plasticity is very close to Synaptic Plasticity under Course › Science › Biology › Neuroscience.

Normalized name collision. Does not block. The two are usually the same thing and occasionally are not, so this is the user's call. FND-77

No parent chosen. This will be created under owl:Thing.

Root level caution. Stated beside the parent row and again in the commit footer, in both places. A user who does not notice they are creating a root level class is the second most common error on this surface. FND-71

GCounts

Two kinds of count with two different meanings. Conflating them is what makes a zero result undiagnosable. FND-31 through FND-36

CountAnswersIgnores
Entity type
Classes 10, Instances 0		 How many entities of this type match now, under the current query and field scope. The entity type scope.
Search field
rdfs:comment 1		 How many entities this field alone would match, whether or not it is currently scoped in. A yield. The field scope.
This changes observed behavior. The shipped build reports field population, not yield: with nothing matching it shows Names and aliases 6,019 and owl:equivalentClass 612, which are counts of entities that have those fields filled in. Neither number answers the question the user has, which is "where is the thing I searched for". shot: 01, shot: 02, FND-35

In the rail below, the query is synaptic plasticity and two fields are scoped in. Both ticked fields report zero. One unticked field reports one. The rail is now telling the user exactly which box to tick.

HRecovery

Below 240 wide, or below 210 high when narrow and 180 otherwise, the pane shows its identity and a way out. Its contents stay mounted but inert, and the query, scope, page and any creation draft survive for the restored pane. FND-104

IBoth themes

Light and dark are authored as two independent token sets. Dark is measured against its own ground, not derived by inverting light. Body text clears 4.5:1 and icons clear 3:1 in both. FND-108

What this file does not show

Keyboard behaviour FND-105, the live region announcing result counts FND-113, commit transaction semantics FND-81 and the copy catalogue FND-116 are all normative and none of them is visible in a still rendering. Read the README for those.
